paper.title: Explore First, Exploit Next: The True Shape of Regret in Bandit Problems

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic K-armed bandit over a general model D (lower bound)
unmapped: arbitrary (possibly non-parametric) model D of distributions with a well-defined expectation
settings.definition_quote: We consider the simplest case of a stochastic bandit problem, with finitely many arms indexed by $a \in \{1,\ldots,K\}$. Each of these arms is associated with an unknown probability distribution $\nu_a$ over~$\R$. We assume that each $\nu_a$ has a well-defined expectation

settings.definition_quote: Consider the bandit model $\mathcal{D} = \mathcal{M}\bigl([0,1]\bigr)$ of all probability distributions over $[0,1]$.

settings.name_in_paper: Two-armed Gaussian bandit, known gap Delta (lower bound)

They consider a bandit model $\mathcal{D}$ containing only sub-Gaussian distributions with parameter $\sigma^2 \leq 1$ ... restrict our attention to the case when $\mu^\star$ is known.

algorithms.name: An algorithm with bounded regret, thanks to the knowledge of mu*

conditions: strategy uniformly fast convergent on D
a is a suboptimal arm

source.label: th:asympt
source.quote: For all models $\mathcal{D}$, for all uniformly fast convergent strategies $\psi$ on $\cD$, for all bandit problems $\unu$, for all suboptimal arms $a$, \[ \liminf_{T \to \infty} \,\, \frac{\E_{\unu} \! \bigl[ N_{\psi,a}(T) \bigr]}{\ln T} \geq \frac{1}{\Kinf(\nu_a,\mu^\star,\cD)}\,. \]

results.notes: Bound on expected pull count of a suboptimal arm (not regret). Re-derivation of Burnetas-Katehakis/Lai-Robbins bound, here for arbitrary models without extra conditions; marked not new.

conditions: strategy smarter than the uniform strategy on D (E[N_{a*}(T)] >= T/K for optimal arms)

source.label: th:2
source.quote: For all models $\cD$, for all strategies $\psi$ that are smarter than the uniform strategy on $\cD$, for all bandit problems~$\unu$, for all arms $a$, for all $T \geq 1$, \[ \E_{\unu} \bigl[ N_{\psi,a}(T) \bigr] \geq \frac{T}{K} \Bigl( 1 - \sqrt{2 T \Kinf(\nu_a,\mu^\star,\cD)} \Bigr)\,. \]

results.notes: Lower bound on expected number of pulls of arm a (absolute lower bound, small T regime).

conditions: strategy smarter than the uniform strategy on D
results.notes: Pull-count lower bound in the initial linear phase.

conditions: strategy pairwise symmetric for optimal arms on D
a suboptimal, a* optimal

source.label: th:3
source.quote: For all models $\cD$, for all strategies $\psi$ that are pairwise symmetric for optimal arms on $\cD$, ... for all $T \geq 1$, \[ \mbox{either} \quad \E_{\unu} \bigl[ N_{\psi,a}(T) \bigr] \geq \frac{T}{K} \qquad \mbox{or} \quad \E_{\unu} \!\!\left[ \frac{\max\bigl\{N_{\psi,a}(T),\,1\bigr\}}{\max\bigl\{N_{\psi,a^\star}(T),\,1\bigr\}} \right] \geq 1 - 2 \sqrt{\frac{2T \, \KL(\nu_a,\nu_{a^\star})}{K}} \,. \]

results.notes: Relative lower bound on the expected ratio of pull counts; the statement is a disjunction (either E[N_a]>=T/K or the ratio bound).

conditions: strategy pairwise symmetric for optimal arms on D

symbols.A_star: number of optimal arms of the problem
symbols.K_max: min over worst arms w of max over optimal arms a* of KL(nu_w, nu_{a*})

conditions: strategy pairwise symmetric for optimal arms and monotonic on D

source.label: th:4
source.quote: For all models $\cD$, for all strategies $\psi$ that are pairwise symmetric for optimal arms and monotonic on $\cD$, for all bandit problems $\unu$ in $\cD$, suboptimal arms are collectively sampled at least \sum_{a \not\in \cA^\star(\unu)} \E_{\unu}\bigl[N_{\psi,a}(T)\bigr]\geq T \Bigg(1-\frac{A^\star_{\unu}}{K} -\frac{A^\star_{\unu} \sqrt{ 2T \, \cK^{\max}_{\unu}}}{K}-\frac{2 A^\star_{\unu} T \cK^{\max}_{\unu}}{K}\Bigg)

results.notes: Collective pull-count lower bound; regret lower bound follows by multiplying by min gap (eq. LBth4).

symbols.K_max: min over worst arms w of max over optimal arms a* of KL(nu_w, nu_{a*})

conditions: strategy pairwise symmetric for optimal arms and monotonic on D

bound.regime: T >= 2 large enough that (ln T)^{-4} < eps_D(mu*) and a_T, b_T, c_T < 1

symbols.b_T: C_psi * H * ln(T)/T, with H = sum over suboptimal arms of 1/Delta_i^2
symbols.C_psi: constant in the uniform super-fast convergence definition E[N_a(T)] <= C_psi ln T / Delta_a^2
symbols.omega_D: local Lipschitz constant of Kinf in the well-behaved model definition

conditions: model D is well behaved (Kinf locally Lipschitz in second argument)
strategy uniformly super-fast convergent on D
a suboptimal

source.label: th:LBlargeT-NA
source.quote: For all uniformly super-fast convergent strategies $\psi$ on well-behaved models $\mathcal{D}$, for all bandit problems $\unu$ in $\mathcal{D}$, for all suboptimal arms $a$, \E_{\unu} \! \bigl[ N_{\psi,a}(T) \bigr] \geq \frac{\ln T}{\Kinf(\nu_a,\mu^\star,\cD)} \bigl( 1 - (a_T + b_T + c_T) \bigr) - \frac{\ln 2}{\Kinf(\nu_a,\mu^\star,\cD)}\,, for all $T \geq 2$ large enough ...

results.notes: Remark: equivalently ln T/Kinf - O(ln ln T).

symbols.eps_gap: gap parameter of the constructed Bernoulli instance (1/2 vs 1/2+eps)

conditions: exists a Bernoulli instance (all arms 1/2 except one at 1/2+eps)

source.label: th:distr-free
source.quote: Consider the bandit model $\mathcal{D} = \mathcal{M}\bigl([0,1]\bigr)$ of all probability distributions over $[0,1]$. For all $\varepsilon \in (0,1/2)$, for all strategies $\psi$, there exists a bandit problem $\unu'$ in $\mathcal{M}\bigl([0,1]\bigr)$ such that \[ R_{\psi,\unu',T} \geq T \varepsilon \left( 1 - \frac{1}{K} - \frac{1}{2} \sqrt{\frac{T}{K} \ln \frac{1}{1-4\varepsilon^2}} \right). \]

results.notes: Re-proof of Theorem A.2 of Auer et al. 2002; consequence sup regret >= (1/20) min(sqrt(KT),T) recorded in cited_results.

conditions: instance (N(0,1), N(-Delta,1))
strategy symmetric: on (N(0,1),N(0,1)) each arm pulled T/2 times in expectation

source.label: th:LB-BPR
source.quote: For all strategies $\psi$ that are symmetric in the sense of~\eqref{eq:sym}, for all $\Delta > 0$, for all $T \geq 1$, \[ \E_{\unu_{\!\Delta}} \! \bigl[ N_{\psi,2}(T) \bigr] \geq \frac{1}{\Delta^2 + 1/T} \qquad \mbox{and} \qquad R_{\psi,\unu_{\!\Delta},T} \geq \frac{\Delta}{\Delta^2 + 1/T}\,. \]

results.notes: Also E[N_2(T)] >= 1/(Delta^2+1/T). Framed as the known-mu* setting (mu*=0).

conditions: instance (N(0,1), N(-Delta,1))

source.label: th:LB-BPR
source.quote: In addition, for all strategies $\psi$ and for all $T$ such that $\E_{\unu_{\!\Delta}} \! \bigl[ N_{\psi,2}(T) \bigr] \geq 1$, ... R_{\psi,\unu_{\!\Delta},T} \geq \min\left\{ \frac{2 (\ln 2) \Delta}{\Delta^2 + 2 \ln(4T)/T}, \,\, \frac{T\Delta}{2} \right\}.

results.notes: Proof uses symmetry assumption (eq:sym) via E_{nu_0}[N_2]=T/2 although statement says all strategies; recorded as stated.

conditions: max over the two instances (N(0,1),N(-Delta,1)) and (N(0,1),N(Delta,1))

source.label: th:LB-BPR2
source.quote: We fix $\Delta > 0$ and consider $\unu_1 = \bigl( \cN(0,1), \, \cN(-\Delta,1) \bigr)$ and $\unu_2 = \bigl( \cN(0,1), \, \cN(\Delta,1) \bigr)$. Then, for all strategies $\psi$, for all $T \geq 1$, \max \bigl\{ R_{\psi,\unu_1,T}, \, R_{\psi,\unu_2,T} \bigr\} \geq \min \! \left\{ \frac{W\bigl(T \Delta^2/1.2\bigr)}{2 \Delta}, \,\, \frac{T\Delta}{2} \right\}.

conditions: strategy symmetric and invariant by translation of the payoffs
instances (N(0,1),N(-Delta,1)) and (N(0,1),N(Delta,1))

source.label: th:LB-BPR2
source.quote: Or, alternatively, for all strategies $\psi$ that are symmetric and invariant by translation of the payoffs, for all $T \geq 1$, \[ R_{\psi,\unu_1,T} = R_{\psi,\unu_2,T} \geq \frac{W\bigl(T \Delta^2/1.2\bigr)}{2 \Delta}\,. \]

conditions: each arm 1-sub-Gaussian (variance proxy <= 1)

source.label: th:finiteRegret:mus:known
source.quote: For all bandit problems $\unu = (\nu_a)_{a = 1,\ldots,K}$ where each distribution $\nu_a$ is sub-Gaussian in the sense of~\eqref{eq:sub-Gaussian}, the regret of the algorithm above is bounded by \[ R_{\unu,T} \leq \sum_{a : \Delta_a > 0} \Biggl( \frac{36\ln(17/\Delta_a)}{\Delta_a} + 3\Delta_a \Biggr). \]

results.notes: Bounded regret independent of T; algorithm does not use T. Paper says refinement already known by Bubeck-Perchet-Rigollet.

not_a_guarantee.comment: The paper says it explicitly re-proves Theorem A.2 of Auer et al. (2002) ('we re-prove Theorem~A.2 of AuCBFrSc02'). This is a restated prior result and belongs in cited_results, which the extractor itself signalled with is_new=false.

_verify.summary: The extraction is accurate: every expression, constant, regime and condition matches the source theorems, and the settings encode the known-mu*/known-gap distinction correctly. The only problem is r9, a re-proof of Auer et al.'s Theorem A.2 that should be a cited result rather than a new result. No performance theorems are missing.
